primary_topics: Address at a Pampanga trial judges convention, October 12, 2006 -- 'my coming home to Pampanga has been oftener in the past few months than it has been collectively in the past two decades'

APJR achievements review: access (Justice on Wheels program, mobile courts, Rules of Court amendments); corruption/incompetence (strict entrance/promotion requirements, ethical education, doubled compensation per RA 9227); delay (Zero Backlog Committee; 48.02% reduction in old SC cases)
The candle-fill-the-room parable: a man with three children gives each P1,000 to fill a room -- the tree doesn't fit, the hay doesn't fill, the candles illuminate the whole room at nightfall

Call to trial judges: 'I urge all of you to take courage in lighting your own little candles of reform in your respective courts and together, we shall light up the firmament of justice in our country'
sub_topics: Context: 'It seems my coming home to Pampanga has been oftener in the past few months than it has been collectively in the past two decades. I am back in Pampanga to grace your convention.'
Vision restatement: four Ins, ACID, safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity -- 'It seems just yesterday when I took my oath as the 21st Chief Justice'

Access to justice: 'the Supreme Court has amended some portions of the Rules of Court'; Justice on Wheels program (December 21, 2004; mobile court with judge, prosecutor, stenographer; first serving Family Court cases in NCR); two more buses ordered for Visayas and Mindanao

Corruption and incompetence: 'strict entrance and promotion requirements; continuing ethical education; and improvement of the compensation of judges'; compensation doubled with full implementation of RA 9227
Delay: created Committee on Zero Backlog upon assuming office; 'percentage of old cases assigned to the three Divisions of the Supreme Court has drastically gone down by 48.02 per cent'

Trial judges as front line: 'the steps taken to address the ACID problems would not amount to much without the involvement of all the members of the bench, particularly those in the front line like all of you. To the vast majority of our people, justice is represented and dispensed by you, the trial judges.'

Candle parable: man with three children; each given P1,000 to fill the room; first child -- big tree (didn't cover room); second -- hay (didn't fill); third -- bought candles and matches, lit them at nightfall; 'the room was filled with light. At the sight of this, the father exclaimed: This is the one who will lead.'

Closing call: 'sometimes it takes so little to accomplish so much of a gargantuan task. I urge all of you to take courage in lighting your own little candles of reform in your respective courts and together, we shall light up the firmament of justice in our country.'

stances.claim: Trial judges are the most important actors in the Philippine justice system because 'to the vast majority of our people, justice is represented and dispensed by you, the trial judges' -- not by the Supreme Court, which is 'distant and far removed from their daily lives.' The APJR's success depends entirely on the willingness of trial judges to implement reforms at the front line.
stances.rhetorical_move: trial-judges-as-true-front-line: the SC's distance vs. trial courts' intimacy with the people as the governing argument for why trial judges matter most
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing institutional insight

notable_anecdotes: Candle-fill-the-room parable: man gives each of three children P1,000 to fill the room; tree too big, hay not filling, candles fill with light at nightfall; 'the father exclaimed: This is the one who will lead' -- applied to trial judges as the candle-lighters of judicial reform.

Justice on Wheels: the first mobile court (December 21, 2004) was a large bus staffed with a judge, prosecutor and stenographer, serving Family Court cases in the NCR; two more buses ordered for Visayas and Mindanao -- the access-to-justice initiative made concrete.

48.02% reduction in old cases: the most specific quantitative achievement cited in any APJR speech -- 'the percentage of old cases assigned to the three Divisions of the Supreme Court has drastically gone down by 48.02 per cent.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered October 12, 2006 at a Pampanga trial judges convention -- 'my coming home to Pampanga has been oftener in the past few months than it has been collectively in the past two decades' -- this address by CJP reviews the APJR achievements of his 10-month tenure. On access to justice: the Justice on Wheels program (deployed December 21, 2004; a mobile court bus with judge, prosecutor and stenographer, initially for Family Court cases in the NCR; two more buses ordered for Visayas and Mindanao). On corruption and incompetence: strict entrance and promotion requirements, continuing ethical education, and doubled compensation per RA 9227. On delay: Zero Backlog Committee created upon assuming office; 'old cases assigned to the three Divisions of the Supreme Court have drastically gone down by 48.02 per cent.' The key insight: 'the SC may be the highest court of the land, but to the vast majority of our people, justice is represented and dispensed by you, the trial judges.' He closes with the candle-fill-the-room parable: a man gives each of three children P1,000 to fill the room; the tree doesn't cover it, the hay doesn't fill it, the third child buys candles and matches -- 'at nightfall, he lit the candles one by one, and slowly the room was filled with light. The father exclaimed: This is the one who will lead.' Application: 'sometimes it takes so little to accomplish so much of a gargantuan task. I urge all of you to take courage in lighting your own little candles of reform in your respective courts and together, we shall light up the firmament of justice in our country.'
